title: On high probability of universal approximation in random basis expansions with non-continuous weight sampling
summary: Random basis expansion (RBE) search the span of a randomly sampled basis to find the best approximation of a target function. They are equivalent to single layer neural networks where the hidden layer weights are chosen randomly. Universal approximation properties have been established for RBEs using continuous weight sampling distributions and real-valued activation functions. Our results extend the universal approximation property to RBEs that use non-continuous weight distributions with dense support in the weight space and that use complex-valued activation functions.
